findings.violation: "e-mail" is not a valid HTML autocomplete token (the correct value is "email"), so browsers will not reliably autofill this field.

findings.fix: Add `minlength="8"` to the confirm-password input to match the password field.
findings.violation: Unlike the password field, this input has no `minlength="8"`, so a user could type a confirmation shorter than the minimum password length with no immediate feedback that something is off.

findings.fix: Make the field optional, or fold it into the street-address field instead of requiring it separately.
findings.violation: Requiring a separate, mandatory "house number" field blocks users whose address has no numbered house (rural addresses, PO boxes, many non-US formats).

findings.fix: Differentiate the tokens, e.g. use `autocomplete="tel"` for the primary and a non-autofilled or `tel-extension`/custom token for the secondary field.
findings.violation: Using the identical autocomplete token for both the primary and secondary phone fields can cause browsers to autofill the same number into both, defeating the purpose of a "secondary" phone.

findings.fix: Remove the field, or make it optional and clearly scoped to business accounts only.
findings.violation: A required "company website" field is out of place on a consumer retail account signup (Meridian Outfitters) and will block individual customers who have no company website.

findings.evidence: `placeholder="Must be 8 digits"` with no `pattern` or `maxlength` attribute
findings.fix: Add `pattern="\d{8}"` and `maxlength="8"` to enforce the stated format.
findings.violation: The "8 digits" requirement is only communicated via placeholder text (which disappears on input) and is not actually enforced, so users can submit the wrong length or non-numeric characters.

findings.evidence: `<label id="acctnum-label" for="acctnum-input">Account number</label>` with no helper text
findings.fix: Add helper text clarifying the field's purpose (e.g., an existing loyalty/catalog account number), or remove it if not needed at signup.
findings.violation: It's unclear what "account number" means for someone who is creating a new account for the first time, and unlike the phone field there's no explanatory text.

findings.evidence: `<input id="postal-input" name="postal_code" type="text" autocomplete="postal-code" required="">` - no corresponding country field anywhere in the form
findings.fix: Add a required country field (e.g., a `select` with `autocomplete="country"`) before or alongside the postal code field.
findings.violation: Postal code format and validity depend on country, but the form never collects a country, which is especially inconsistent given "International" is offered as a shipping option.

findings.fix: Remove the duplicate "Next-day"/"Overnight" option and move "International" out of this speed selector into a destination/country-driven field.
findings.violation: "Overnight" and "Next-day" are redundant options that will confuse users, and "International" conflates a shipping destination with a shipping speed.

findings.evidence: `<label id="legalname-label" for="legalname-input">Your name</label> ... autocomplete="name"` versus the earlier `row-name` field `<label id="name-label" for="name-input">Full name</label> ... autocomplete="name"`
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate "Your name" field, or rename/repurpose it to clarify how it differs from "Full name" (e.g., legal name for billing vs. display name).
findings.violation: The form asks for the user's name twice (full_name and legal_name), both marked `autocomplete="name"`, which is redundant and may cause browser autofill to populate them inconsistently.

findings.fix: Make the field optional and only show/require it for business account signups.
findings.violation: A required organization name field is inappropriate for an individual consumer creating a retail account and forces non-business users to invent a value.

findings.fix: Replace with a `<select>` of discrete time ranges or a `type="time"` input, and remove the hard requirement.
findings.violation: A free-text required field for "preferred contact time" gives no format guidance, so submissions will be inconsistent ("morning", "9am", "anytime") and hard to use programmatically.

findings.evidence: `<button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button>` - document contains no `<script>` element
findings.fix: Either remove the button or add the script/handler that implements its "View details" behavior.
findings.violation: The button has `type="button"` (so it won't submit the form) but there is no JavaScript anywhere in the document to give it behavior, making it a dead control.

findings.evidence: `<select id="hear-select" required="">` for "How did you hear about us?"
findings.fix: Remove the `required` attribute from this select.
findings.violation: Marketing-attribution questions are not essential to account creation and requiring an answer adds friction/blocks submission for users who don't fit the listed options.

findings.fix: Move these styles into a stylesheet with classes applied consistently across equivalent elements.
findings.location: Throughout the form (e.g. org-input, contacttime-label, viewdetails-btn)
findings.violation: Styling is applied ad hoc via inline `style` attributes on only a few scattered elements rather than consistently through CSS, making the presentation inconsistent and hard to maintain.

findings.evidence: No `<fieldset>`/`<legend>` elements anywhere in the document
findings.fix: Wrap related field groups (name/contact, address, account/shipping preferences) in `<fieldset>` elements with descriptive `<legend>` labels.
findings.violation: Related fields (e.g. house number, street, postal code) are not grouped semantically, which hurts accessibility and makes the long flat list of fields harder to scan.
